name: autockpt
_comment: Does re-enabling auto-checkpoint help, and what does it cost?
No second binary is needed: wal_autocheckpoint is already a harness axis, so
one BF build is swept across it and compared with stock at its own default.
That keeps the comparison inside one campaign, which is the only kind this
repo has found trustworthy (identical code has spanned 9913/11652/8102 ops/s
What to read, in this order -- throughput alone cannot answer this:
WAL B/commit      a checkpoint converts buffered records into base-page
writes, so the Phase-2 '1 page frame per commit' story
changes shape; if this rises a lot, the win is paid for
pg frames/commit  the same thing seen from the record side
read bytes/op     the reason to do this at all: an unbounded WAL makes
every read search a larger wal-index (walFindFrame was
ops/s             last, and only next to its spread
autocheckpoint=0 is today's forced BF behaviour; 1000 is SQLite's default;
10000 is there to show whether the interesting variable is 'bounded at all'

experiments.name: read_after_writes
_why: A pure read workload never grows the WAL, so it cannot show the
cost being removed.  This one writes 20% of the time, which is
what makes the wal-index grow under autocheckpoint=0.
